'''Ujiyamada Shrine''' (宇治山田神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Inner Shrine) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It is located on a small hill locally known as Okutama no Mori (興玉の森).<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.106</ref>
This article also covers '''Najime Shrine''' (那自賣神社), which shares the same site as Ujiyamada Shrine.
== Overview ==
This section describes common features of both shrines.
The shrines are situated at the southwestern edge of the Nakamura {{ill|Human settlement|en|Human settlement|qid=Q486972|lt=settlement}} in {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}.<ref name="sk">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.253</ref> The shrine grounds cover 4 tan and 5 se (approximately 4,463 m<sup>2</sup>).<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.10</ref> Both shrines are said to have been established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|ja|弥姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamatohime-no-mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.<ref name="ic"/>
The {{ill|Shinto architecture|ja|社殿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/shaden|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神社建築|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3080012}} is built in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style and is surrounded by a {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} as shown in the photo. There is no {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/saisenbako|qid=Q135491444}}. The area around the shrine is covered with moss.<ref name="ic"/>
== Ujiyamada Shrine ==
Ujiyamada Shrine Ranks 13th among the 33 sessha of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy"/> The {{ill|saijin|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/saijin|qq=}} is Yodahime-no-Mikoto (山田比賣命),<ref name="uy"/> also known as Yamada-hime-no-Mikoto.<ref name="ic"/> She is considered a water deity, said to be the child of Ōminakami no Kami (大水上神).<ref name="ic"/>
Together with {{ill|Katada Shrine|ja|堅田神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katada Shrine|qq=}}, another sessha of the Inner Shrine, it is considered a candidate for the "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine" (大國玉比賣神社) mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}.<ref name="sk"/>
== Najime Shrine ==
Najime Shrine Ranks 13th among the 16 massha of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy2">Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.14</ref> The enshrined deities are Ōminakami no Mioya no Mikoto (大水上御祖命)<ref name="uy2"/> and Mimonosuso-hime no Mikoto (御裳乃須蘇比賣命).<ref name="uy2"/> Both are considered water guardians of the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}.<ref name="ic"/> Mimonosuso-hime no Mikoto is traditionally regarded as the spirit of Ōminakami no Kami.<ref name="ik">Ise City Tourism Association</ref> The main shrine has ceased to exist, and Najime Shrine is now co-located with Ujiyamada Shrine.<ref name="uy2"/>
== History ==
The Ōkunidama-hime Shrine mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} is considered a candidate for Ujiyamada Shrine, although it is not mentioned in the "Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō" and no shrine with the same name exists in modern Ise or Watarai District.<ref name="sk"/>
In 1874, the shrine buildings of Ujiyamada Shrine, along with {{ill|Kamoshimo Shrine|ja|鴨下神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamoshimo Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsubura Shrine|ja|津布良神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubura Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)|lt=Ōtsu Shrine|ja|大津神社 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtsu Shrine (Ise)|qq=}} were reconstructed.<ref>Sakurai (1991): pp.280-281</ref> Ujiyamada Shrine was rebuilt again in 1911 and underwent major repairs in 1959, with another relocation ceremony held in 2018.<ref name="uy"/>
== Surroundings ==
Located within the Nakamura settlement.<ref name="sk"/> The entrance to the shrine is somewhat difficult to find despite Okutama no Mori being a noticeable hill.<ref name="ic"/> Nearby flows the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}, and beyond the Osoba Bridge is Isuzu Park.
